note: When no CPU model is specified, the default model qemu64 is selected, which has hardcoded cpuid values defined in builtin_x86_defs.
The CPU definition is taken from the static builtin_x86_defs array, which contains hardcoded cpuid_level, cpuid_version, vendor, and feature values rather than querying the host CPU.
The cpuid level and extended level are set from the hardcoded CPU model definition (level=0xd for qemu64), not from the actual host CPU capabilities.

code: x86_cpuid_version_set_family(cpu, def->family); x86_cpuid_version_set_model(cpu, def->model); x86_cpuid_version_set_stepping(cpu, def->stepping);
note: The CPUID version (family/model/stepping) is hardcoded from the model definition (family=6, model=6, stepping=3 for qemu64) instead of being read from the actual CPU.

code: for (w = 0; w < FEATURE_WORDS; w++) { env->features[w] = def->features[w]; }
note: All CPU feature flags are copied from the hardcoded model definition, so the emulated CPU reports features that may not match the host CPU.
The CPUID vendor string is set from the hardcoded model definition (CPUID_VENDOR_AMD for qemu64) rather than from the actual host CPU vendor.
When guest code executes the CPUID instruction, the helper calls cpu_x86_cpuid which returns the hardcoded values from the model definition instead of querying the host CPU.
The CPUID index is clamped to the hardcoded cpuid_level (0xd for qemu64), so any request for CPUID leaves beyond this level returns the hardcoded level value.
CPUID leaf 0 returns the hardcoded maximum level (0xd) and the hardcoded AMD vendor string, which may not match the actual host CPU vendor or capabilities.
CPUID leaf 1 returns the hardcoded version (family 6, model 6, stepping 3) and hardcoded feature flags, which may not match the actual host CPU and can lead to incorrect behavior in guest software.

code: env->regs[R_EAX] = eax; env->regs[R_EBX] = ebx; env->regs[R_ECX] = ecx; env->regs[R_EDX] = edx;
note: The hardcoded CPUID results are written back into the guest registers, so any guest code that relies on CPUID to detect CPU features will receive incorrect information about the emulated CPU.
